messages:
eva: Noticed a weird graph on the console: p95 > p99 for /v1/chat in us-east for ~10m. p50/p95 fine everywhere else. anyone seen this inversion before?

jon: huh that shouldn't be possible mathematically. usually p99 >= p95. could be a display/aggregation bug.

monitor-bot: Metric anomaly detected: p95(%) for /v1/chat (us-east) increased from 120ms to 980ms between 11:02-11:12 UTC. p99(%) reported at 850ms.

samir: my money is on rollup merge semantics. we recently started stitching low-sample rollups using tdigest summaries, might be merging incompatible summaries (different quantile compression params).

yuki: I ran a samples check: ```sql
SELECT sample_origin, quantile_type, percentile(latency_ms,95) p95, percentile(latency_ms,99) p99, count(*)
FROM telemetry_latency
WHERE route='/v1/chat' AND region='us-east' AND time >= now() - interval '30 minutes'
GROUP BY sample_origin, quantile_type
ORDER BY count DESC;
```

eva: results: sample_origin=frontend-proxy, quantile_type=tdigest_c=100 -> p95=920 p99=880 count=12; sample_origin=backend, quantile_type=tdigest_c=50 -> p95=110 p99=150 count=540. The merged rollup shows p95~450 p99~380.

jon: aha: tdigest with different compression c produces incompatible sketches; naive merge doesn't guarantee monotonic quantiles. merging c=100 with c=50 can give non-monotonic outputs. we should be normalizing or refusing merges across differing compression parameters.

samir: yeah we have a bug in rollup-merge: we only check sketch type, not compression param. fix options: (1) avoid merging sketches with different compression and keep separate slices; (2) recompute exact quantiles from raw samples when counts small; (3) normalize by reserializing to a common compression before merging (expensive).

yuki: small-sample front proxy (count=12) dominated the p95 in the merged summary because its higher p95 dragged the blended value up. since counts are small, (2) sounds attractive: backfill exact quantiles for windows where any contributing slice has count<50.

eva: agree. short-term I prefer: mark merges as "incompatible" and fall back to showing per-slice badges in UI + an annotation explaining the mismatch. long-term pick (2) or (3) depending on CPU cost.

jon: I'll open a patch to add a merge guard: if sketch_type==tdigest and compression differs, flag as incompatible and store each sketch separately. UI will compute a conservative rollup (weighted median?) until we do exact recompute.

samir: add a telemetry counter so we can alert when incompatible merges happen often. also add a dashboard tooltip that says "rollup contains mixed sketch compressions; quantiles may be non-monotonic".

yuki: I'll prototype the exact-recompute job outline (RT-4501). it will kick for windows where any contributing slice has count < 100 and compute quantiles from raw samples in batch.

eva: nice. for immediate mitigation can we backfill the last 2h for the affected window and flip a console annotation so customers aren't freaked out?

jon: pushing the guard to canary now. will add UI annotation and telemetry counter in the same PR.

monitor-bot: Canary deploy: rollup-merge-guard v1.2 -> enabled for 15% traffic at 11:28 UTC.

eva: thanks. folks, small follow-up: update runbook with a section "tdigest merges" and include links to RT-4501 + the UI ticket. otherwise we'll keep re-hunting this. :book:
